title: School council

for: It's **more useful than you'd think**: loads of medical and legal words come from Latin.
**It was hard, but it paid off** — Spanish and Italian were much easier for me later.
against: **What's the point of** Latin? Nobody speaks it.
I did five years of it, and **I've never used it since**.

for: It's **more useful than you'd think** — it's everywhere in films, books and even brand names.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — in a quiz, for example.
against: It's fun, but the way it's taught is **out of touch with real life** — just names to memorise.
**You pick it up along the way** — from films and games.

for: **Back in my day**, we learned poems **by heart**, and it was great memory training.
**It was hard, but it paid off**: I still know some of them, and they mean a lot to me.
against: **It was a complete waste of time** — I can't remember a single line now.
**What's the point of** learning poems by heart when you can look them up in two seconds?

for: It's **more useful than you'd think**: key dates help you put events in order and see how they're connected.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — like when your kids need help with their homework.
against: We learned hundreds of dates **by heart**, but never talked about why they mattered — **a complete waste of time**.
**What's the point of** memorising dates? You can look them up.

for: **You never know when it might come in handy** — you might end up as an engineer or a game designer.
**It was hard, but it paid off** when I studied engineering.
against: **I've never used it since** — not once.
**It was out of touch with real life** — we never knew what it was for.

for: It's **more useful than you'd think** — it helps explain why things burn, rust or explode.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — you might end up working in a lab.
against: We learned the whole table **by heart**, and **I've never used it since**.
The way we learned it **was out of touch with real life** — just symbols and numbers.

for: It comes up **more often than you'd think** — in documentaries, in your kids' homework, in the news.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — like when a doctor explains your test results.
against: We did cell biology for a whole year, and **I've never used it since**.
**What's the point of** it, unless you want to be a doctor?

for: **Nobody ever taught us how to** make a budget, and my first credit card was a disaster.
It's **more important than you'd think** — one bad loan can leave you in debt for years.
against: **You pick it up along the way**, like everyone does.
**What's the point of** a school subject? Every family handles money differently.

for: **You never know when it might come in handy** — it can save a life.
**Nobody ever taught us how to** help someone who's choking.
against: **School only gets you so far** — if you don't practise it, you forget it within a year.
**My kids' school is very hands-on** — they already have a first-aid day every year.

for: **Nobody ever taught us how to** cook, so I lived on pasta for a year.
**My kids' school is very hands-on** — they cook every Friday, and they love it.
against: **You pick it up along the way** — from your parents or from YouTube.
**Back in my day**, we had cooking classes, but we spent most of the lesson waiting for the oven — **a complete waste of time**.

for: **Nobody ever taught us how to** do our taxes, and my first tax return took a whole weekend.
It's **more complicated than you'd think**, so everyone needs at least the basics.
against: **What's the point of** teaching it at fifteen? The rules change every year.
When we moved abroad, **I had to start from scratch** — the tax system was completely different.

for: **It was hard, but it paid off**: I type twice as fast as my colleagues.
It's **more useful than you'd think** — we all type all day.
against: **You pick it up along the way** — there are free apps for it, so why make it a school subject?
It's a bit **out of touch with real life** — kids do everything on their phones now.

for: Explaining an idea so that people get it — **that's where I really add value** at work.
**Nobody ever taught us how to** speak in front of people, and I was terrified for years.
against: **What's the point of** making every shy kid give speeches?
**School only gets you so far** — confidence comes from doing it for real, not from one lesson a week.

for: It's **more useful than you'd think** — every flat has a dripping tap or a wobbly shelf.
**My kids' school is very hands-on**, and the kids love it — repairs would fit right in.
against: **You pick it up along the way** — YouTube has a video for everything.
**Back in my day**, people learned it from their parents, not at school.
